head.meta_description: Iftar catering trends for Ramadan 2026 in Dubai: shared buffets, live stations, elevated Arabic menus, slow-energy suhoor and corporate iftars, with real dates, timings and food-safety facts.
head.h1: Ramadan & Iftar Catering Trends 2026 — Real Prices and Timings

opening_paragraph: Dubai's biggest iftar catering trends for 2026 are generous shared buffets, elevated Arabic menus and a serious suhoor, with myCHEF planning iftar buffets from AED 120 a head. The season rewards hosts who book early and brief a chef who knows the rhythm of the fast.

new_paragraphs: Want these iftar catering trends turned into one plan, explained end to end? Start with your date and guest count. Whether you search "iftar catering near me" or come straight to us, our Ramadan services cover the full arc of the month: iftar , Ramadan and suhoor , with halal menus and timed service to Maghrib. You can also begin at private chef or catering in Dubai .
When did Ramadan 2026 start in the UAE?
Ramadan 2026 started on Wednesday 18 February, after the crescent moon was sighted on 17 February. The month ran about 29 days, so plan your iftars around that window.
What time is iftar served during Ramadan?
Iftar is served at sunset, immediately after the Maghrib call to prayer. Your caterer should have dates, water and soup ready the moment the Ramadan cannon sounds.
How far ahead should I book iftar catering in Dubai?
Book three to four weeks ahead, and earlier for the first weekend and the last ten nights. Those dates are the season's busiest and fill first.
Is myCHEF iftar catering halal?
Yes. Arabic and halal iftar menus are led by chef Layla Hassan, and you can confirm sourcing and the caterer's Dubai Municipality food permit before booking.
What is trending for corporate iftars in 2026?
Larger, earlier, fully staffed events. Shorter Ramadan working days mean companies host proper team iftars with timed service instead of a drop-off buffet.
How much should an iftar spread cost per person?

Plan from around AED 120 a head for a shared drop-off buffet, about AED 150 with live stations, and AED 700 to 950 once chefs cook and serve on site all evening. Ask for a written proposal to compare fairly.
What is the most popular food for iftar?

Dates and water come first, always, followed by soup, usually lentil. After that the most popular iftar dishes in Dubai are samosas, stuffed vine leaves, fattoush and fresh juices, then grilled meats and a rice dish such as machboos, biryani or harees. Kunafa and qatayef close it.
How do I arrange an iftar party at home?

Fix the date, count back three to four weeks, and brief your caterer on headcount, venue, halal requirements and dietary needs in writing. Then build the evening backwards from Maghrib: setup about two hours before sunset, dates and water ready the moment the fast breaks, mains after prayer.

add_block.new_heading: What are the biggest iftar catering trends for 2026?
new_paragraphs: The headline iftar catering trends this year are scale and design. Hosts want a generous shared table, not a plated set menu: mezze, grills, slow-cooked rice, and live carving or shawarma stations that keep the room moving after Maghrib. Arabic classics sit next to international dishes, so a mixed guest list finds something familiar. The majlis-style setup is back in a considered form, with low seating, warm lighting, and dates and laban within reach. If you are hunting for iftar party ideas in Dubai, the best ones this Ramadan lean on abundance, movement and a clear opening moment. That opening moment matters more than any single dish on the spread.

add_block.new_heading: When is Ramadan 2026, and why does the booking date matter?
new_paragraphs: Ramadan 2026 began on Wednesday 18 February, confirmed by the UAE moon-sighting committee after the crescent was seen on the evening of 17 February, as reported by Khaleej Times . Dubai's Islamic Affairs department issued a 29-day calendar, with fasting close to 13 hours and stretching toward 13 and a half near the end of the month. Why does this matter to you? The first weekend and the final ten nights are the busiest iftar windows in the city, and popular dates disappear first. Treat the confirmed start as your planning anchor: count back three to four weeks and lock your caterer then. Late bookings still happen, but menu and staffing choices narrow fast.

add_block.new_heading: How does iftar timing shape the menu and service?
new_paragraphs: Iftar is eaten at sunset, right after the Maghrib call to prayer, and in the UAE the fast is opened with dates and water before anything heavier, as What's On Dubai explains. Sunset itself is marked by the Ramadan cannon, fired to precise daily timings. For catering, that single sunset moment is the whole brief. Dates, water, laban and soup need to be ready the instant the cannon sounds, with appetizers such as samosas and stuffed vine leaves following within minutes, then the mains. A good iftar menu in Dubai is built backwards from Maghrib, not forwards from a fixed clock. Timing, not just the food, is what your guests remember.

add_block.new_heading: What is trending for suhoor this Ramadan?
new_paragraphs: Suhoor is being taken more seriously in 2026, and the trend is slow energy instead of a heavy late feast. The pre-dawn meal is eaten before the Fajr prayer, so the job is to carry guests through a long fasting day. Hosts are asking for balanced plates: laban, fresh fruit, eggs, oats, slow-release grains and lighter proteins, styled as a proper occasion instead of an afterthought. Foul, shakshuka, and cheese with olives stay popular, alongside plenty of water. If you host a late-night gathering, a considered suhoor spread is one of the season's quieter but fastest-growing ideas. It reads as care, and guests notice.

add_block.new_heading: How are corporate iftars changing in 2026?
new_paragraphs: Corporate iftars are getting larger and more deliberate. Under Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021, private-sector working hours drop by two a day during Ramadan, from eight to six, with no cut to pay, per the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation . Shorter days push corporate iftars earlier and turn them into genuine team and client events. That means full-service catering, professional floor staff, and service timed to Maghrib instead of a drop-off left on a side table. Share your headcount, venue and any dietary needs early. A corporate iftar checklist that fixes date, timing and halal requirements up front keeps the evening calm.

add_block.new_heading: How do you vet an iftar caterer's food safety?
new_paragraphs: Start with the licence. Dubai treats every catering company as a food establishment, and each must hold a Permit for Food Related Activities from the Dubai Municipality Food Safety Department before it handles a single tray, under the Dubai Food Code , which now leans hard on allergen disclosure and traceability. Ask any caterer to confirm their permit and how they handle halal sourcing. At myCHEF, every chef clears identity checks, a practical cooking assessment, reference verification and ongoing reviews before working an event. For Ramadan, Arabic and halal menus are led by chef Layla Hassan, who builds iftar and suhoor spreads around the tradition instead of a generic buffet template.

add_block.new_heading: How much does iftar catering cost in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: Cost depends on format, headcount and service level, so treat any single figure as a starting point. As a rough guide, a relaxed drop-off or self-serve family iftar plans from around AED 120 per guest, and a premium spread with live carving or shawarma stations from about AED 150. Once chefs cook and serve on site through the evening you are buying a private-chef service rather than a buffet, and that sits at AED 700 to 950 a head. Larger corporate iftars are usually quoted as a whole event instead of per plate. MyCHEF works to a minimum of 10 guests on volume formats, 20 on a buffet, and a minimum order of AED 900. Prices in Dubai move with menu length, staffing and venue, not with a fixed rate card. The honest way to compare tips and quotes is a written proposal: share your date, numbers and venue, and read each line before you commit.

add_block.new_heading: What are the current trends in the catering industry?
new_paragraphs: Iftar sits inside a wider shift, and most of what is changing across the Dubai catering industry shows up on a Ramadan table first. Live and interactive stations keep spreading, because guests would rather watch a dish finished in front of them than queue at a chafing tray. Allergen and sourcing disclosure has moved from a courtesy to an expectation, pushed by the Food Code's weight on disclosure and traceability. Buyers now compare written per-head prices instead of accepting one lump sum, which is why the gap between a drop-off buffet from AED 120 per person and a staffed evening at AED 700 to 950 is the first thing most enquiries ask about. Quantities are planned tighter, sized to a confirmed headcount rather than over-ordered out of habit. And the year has hardened into two peaks that draw on the same chefs, staff and equipment: Ramadan, and the December festive season when Christmas catering in Dubai books out. Leave either one late and the constraint is rarely the menu, it is the people.

add_block.new_heading: How to arrange an iftar party
new_paragraphs: Arranging an iftar is unlike arranging any other dinner, because the start time is not yours to choose. Everything below is built around that.
Fix the date before anything else. Check whether your night falls in the first weekend or the last ten nights, the two windows that sell out first, and count back three to four weeks from it.
Settle the headcount and the venue. A shared iftar works from 10 guests, and a buffet spread needs 20 to earn its length; below that a plated dinner reads better than a half-empty table.
Work backwards from Maghrib. Look up sunset for your exact date, then set the kitchen's arrival about two hours earlier so the opening plates are standing ready rather than being finished.
Plan the opening moment. Dates, water, laban and soup go out the instant the fast breaks, appetisers follow within minutes, and mains come once the room has settled after prayer.
Put halal requirements and dietary needs in writing when you book, not in the last 48 hours, and ask the caterer to confirm sourcing back to you.
Confirm the menu about seven days out with final numbers, and add 5% VAT when you compare the total against another quote.
